source: Atiqot 41 Part 1, Wexler, 'Preface' (file 02), Table 1 'The sites surveyed and excavated' (PDF p. 13), read from the page image; text pp. ix-x (PDF pp. 9-10)

table_notes.XIV: 61 numbered, plus 3 unnumbered caves in the marl area
table_notes.V_VII: note 6: in some survey descriptions caves were numbered but not described; counted with the caves without remains
table_notes.XII_XV: note 7: no survey description for Regions XII and XV; only the excavations published in the volume are tabulated
table_notes.II: note 4: caves 20-31/II, 33-41/II and 52-60/II were not surveyed systematically

text_statements: More than 495 cave-sites were surveyed; some natural spaces were not numbered separately and sometimes not examined (p. ix, paraphrase).
Subtracting 17 non-cave sites (plots, cisterns, buildings, a kiln, retaining walls, other) leaves more than 478 caves (p. ix, paraphrase).
The SPNI Cave Research Center (Malham) surveyed and mapped many caves in wide parts of the Judean Desert, published case by case in Niqrot Zurim (note 4, paraphrase).

Earlier surveys named: Aharoni (Ein Gedi), Bar-Adon emergency survey, Cross and Milik (Buqeia, Region IX southwards), Marcus, Hirschfeld (Herodium area and beyond), Goldfus and Golani (upper Wadi el-Mabuk), Patrich (Hyrcania valley; much unpublished), Sion (Kalia and Wadi el-Qelt) (pp. ix-x, paraphrase).
